title: Grateful Dead Live at Onondaga County War Memorial on 1973-09-17
lineage: MR > C>DAT>DAT provided by Jeff Tiedrich>Andrew Gustin Conversion: DA-40>U2A>CDWave>MkW with seek tables appended Transferred by Tyler Jensen

ai_review.summary: High‑quality soundboard capture of a 1973 show that dazzles with horns, a stellar Weather Report Suite and standout versions of Sugar Magnolia and Looks Like Rain.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its clear soundboard fidelity, though a few listeners note occasional slicing and missing song intros. Musically the concert shines – Jerry’s vocal on Sugar Magnolia and his soaring leads in the Weather Report Suite are highlighted, the horn section adds a funky jazz edge throughout, and rare moments like Keith’s Theremin solo on Looks Like Rain make it unforgettable.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4‑5 stars, lauding both performance (horns, Weather Report Suite, standout songs) and recording quality; only minor complaints about slicing and a few song issues keep the rating just shy of perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Several reviewers call the sound "great" and note the crispness of a typical 1973 soundboard, but one mentions the tape being "diced & sliced" with missing song beginnings and occasional level problems on Loser.

standout_songs: Weather Report Suite / Let It Grow
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set packs scorching numbers but suffers from a few cuts and level hiccups; the second set blossoms with horn‑driven jams, an extended Weather Report Suite, and jazzy improvisations that give the concert its signature 1973 funk‑jazz vibe.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Powerful vocal lead on Sugar Magnolia and expressive guitar leads in the Weather Report Suite; praised for his presence though one reviewer described his playing as "evil carnival".
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s vocals stumble on a few lyrics (e.g., Truckin') but his rhythm work remains solid throughout.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux shines with a surprising Theremin solo on Looks Like Rain and blends smoothly with the horn section.
